title: CI/CD y seguridad de la cadena de suministro

findings.issue: S44 requires S43, but the preceding S43 audit remains REPAIR_REQUIRED with unresolved P0 blockers.
findings.impact: The release-engineering lesson assumes a trustworthy container/service artifact that the prerequisite has not demonstrated.
findings.improvement: Keep S44 locked until S43 critical blockers are closed or explicitly teach the prerequisite evidence as provisional.

findings.issue: portfolio_ready trusts four learner-editable booleans and gate_case hard-codes normal/breach/uncertain outcomes without reading ARTIFACTS.
findings.impact: A learner can manufacture READY and apparently correct gate routes without a workflow, SBOM, provenance, canary or rollback evidence.
findings.improvement: Parse and verify the actual workflow/SBOM/provenance/canary files; derive every gate result from those artifacts.

findings.issue: Roadmap environment is controlled CI/cloud, but all eight I Do demonstrations declare local-python and the 24 We Do tasks are Python predicates/parsers.
findings.impact: The learner never observes a real workflow run, artifact upload/download, environment gate, attestation verification or rollback evidence before the independent project.
findings.improvement: Retain local models as first scaffold, then fade into an actual CI workflow fixture and downloaded evidence before You Do.

findings.issue: Multiple validators accept any string beginning sha256:, including sha256:def, sha256:abc and sha256:x, as a digest.
findings.impact: Malformed identifiers are taught as cryptographic evidence and can pass promotion.
findings.improvement: Require ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ and bind it to a measured artifact.

findings.issue: Artifact evidence is represented by a supplied digest string rather than hashing or verifying the artifact.
findings.impact: The evidence can describe a file that never existed or whose content differs.
findings.improvement: Hash a produced fixture artifact and verify the stored digest after re-download.

findings.issue: retention_days >= 7 is presented as a general promotion criterion without deriving the period from policy, investigation window or capstone needs.
findings.impact: Creates false precision and confuses a lab parameter with an industry rule.
findings.improvement: Label seven days as CASO-PIU-044 policy and require an explicit retention policy input.

findings.issue: Cache key uses only the first eight characters of a supplied lock hash and never demonstrates that the value is the actual lockfile hash.
findings.impact: The cache can collide or drift from dependency state while still appearing contract-compliant.
findings.improvement: Compute a full digest of the lockfile plus relevant runtime dimensions; keep cache non-authoritative.

findings.issue: Release-path condition coverage is reduced to booleans/string labels rather than inspecting workflow triggers and job if expressions.
findings.impact: A bypass path on tags, forks or manual dispatch can remain invisible.
findings.improvement: Parse a real workflow and test main/tag/PR/fork/manual cases explicitly.

findings.issue: The permission/action-pin figure is attached to T1-A lint/types/tests rather than the T2-A hardening concept it depicts.
findings.impact: Visual guidance arrives before its concept and weakens figure-text coherence.
findings.improvement: Move S44-permission-scope to T2-A; keep the supply-chain pipeline figure with T1.

findings.issue: Any secret_scan hit is mapped to REVOKE_AND_ROTATE, ignoring false positives, synthetic/test credentials, validation status and audited bypass workflows.
findings.impact: Learners conflate detection with confirmed credential compromise and learn the wrong incident response routing.
findings.improvement: Block first; classify/validate the finding; revoke/rotate confirmed active exposed credentials; record approved false-positive/test-secret disposition.

findings.issue: Permission validation is substring-based and does not model effective workflow/job permissions required by attestation jobs.
findings.impact: A workflow can be declared least-privilege without demonstrating the authority actually used by each job.
findings.improvement: Parse YAML structure and check effective permissions per job, including explicit id-token/attestations permissions where provenance is generated.

findings.issue: pin_ok is overwritten for every uses line; a final pinned action makes an earlier unpinned third-party action disappear from the verdict.
findings.impact: A vulnerable workflow can pass the lesson's hardening validator.
findings.counterexample: evil/action@v1 followed by a full-SHA actions/checkout returns pinned=True.
findings.improvement: Collect every uses reference and require every non-local action to satisfy the pin policy.

findings.issue: A 40-hex ref is accepted without verifying that the commit belongs to the intended action repository rather than a fork or unrelated object.
findings.impact: Format validation is mistaken for provenance validation.
findings.improvement: Teach repository+commit verification and retain the resolved action identity as evidence.

findings.issue: dependency_review is a supplied boolean rather than evidence from a dependency review check/report.
findings.impact: A critical supply-chain gate is self-attested.
findings.improvement: Use a stored dependency-review result/fixture and verify its conclusion and policy threshold.

findings.issue: The lesson requires artifact digest == SBOM digest == provenance subject. An SBOM document has its own content digest; what must bind is the SBOM/provenance subject identity to the artifact, not equality of the SBOM file hash with the artifact hash.
findings.impact: Teaches a materially incorrect evidence model and can reject valid SBOMs while accepting fabricated equal strings.
findings.improvement: Represent artifact_digest, sbom_document_digest, sbom_subject_digest and provenance_subject_digest separately; compare subject digests to the artifact.

findings.issue: Attestation validity is supplied as a boolean.
findings.impact: Cryptographic verification is replaced by self-assertion.
findings.improvement: Verify an attestation fixture with expected subject digest, issuer/builder identity and source workflow.

findings.issue: The provenance gate does not inspect builder identity, workflow/repository, source revision or attestation authenticity despite teaching those concepts.
findings.impact: Matching strings can pass even when provenance came from the wrong builder/source.
findings.improvement: Verify subject + trusted builder/issuer + repo + workflow + commit/revision.

findings.issue: Provenance is described as recording 'en qué máquina' in a way that overstates what generic provenance guarantees.
findings.impact: Learners may expect physical runner identity rather than attested builder/workflow/environment metadata.
findings.improvement: Say builder/runtime/workflow identity and recorded build environment information according to the attestation format.

findings.issue: bool(approved_by) is treated as independent approval.
findings.impact: The author can type their own name or any arbitrary string and pass promotion.
findings.improvement: Model initiator, approved_by and allowed reviewer set; require approved_by != initiator and a verified environment approval record.

findings.issue: Environment protection is represented as a list of names/approvers rather than enforcement such as required reviewers/prevent-self-review/branch policy.
findings.impact: The learner can confuse configuration documentation with an enforced deployment gate.
findings.improvement: Inspect an environment policy fixture or CI evidence showing the job waited for and received an authorized review.

findings.issue: Promotion accepts malformed prefix-only sha256 values.
findings.impact: Same-string equality is insufficient if neither string is a valid measured digest.
findings.improvement: Validate full digest and verify it against the staged artifact before promotion.

findings.issue: The section alternates prod and production in environment contracts and examples.
findings.impact: Adds needless schema/terminology friction in an otherwise strict string-based exercise family.
findings.improvement: Choose one canonical environment identifier and distinguish display label from machine value.

findings.issue: No lower-bound validation exists for error rate, rollback seconds or RTO; negative values pass.
findings.impact: Nonsensical telemetry can authorize release.
findings.improvement: Validate 0<=error<=1, 0<=max<=1, rollback_s>=0 and rto>0 before evaluating policy.

findings.issue: The final canary helper omits migration_compatible and rollback_tested even though T3-B teaches both as required.
findings.impact: You Do is weaker than its own guided practice and can pass an untested rollback.
findings.improvement: Carry the full T3-B contract into the final verifier.

findings.issue: Rollback is timed but not bound to a previous known-good digest/config/data state.
findings.impact: A fast action can be called rollback without proving restoration of the intended version.
findings.improvement: Record before_digest, failed_digest, restored_digest and assert restored_digest==last_known_good, plus migration/data recovery evidence.

findings.issue: migration_compatible and rollback_tested are learner-supplied booleans rather than test outputs.
findings.impact: The highest-risk release properties remain self-attested.
findings.improvement: Run compatibility/rollback fixture checks and retain their logs/results.

findings.issue: A single error-rate threshold is treated as sufficient canary evidence without minimum sample/window or other health signals.
findings.impact: At Level 4, learners may infer that a tiny sample below threshold is enough to expand traffic.
findings.improvement: Make the lab contract require a measurement window/sample count and at least one additional SLO signal, while labeling the simplification.

findings.issue: Branch protection, required checks and reviews are modeled by values/sets, not by an enforceable repository policy or evidence snapshot.
findings.impact: Governance becomes descriptive rather than verified.
findings.improvement: Audit a branch/ruleset fixture or exported policy and assert required checks/review count/bypass policy.

findings.issue: signed_commits appears in branch_policy code but is not consistently part of the stated contract or subsequent assessment.
findings.impact: Creates a decorative security signal that learners cannot tell is required, optional or unrelated.
findings.improvement: Either teach and assess commit/tag signing explicitly or remove it from the gate example.

findings.issue: Notes are reduced to presence of four labels, not actionable content, owner/effective migration command, verification or rollback target.
findings.impact: A release note containing empty headings can pass.
findings.improvement: Require minimally structured nonempty values and link rollback to the tested prior digest/runbook.

findings.issue: PASS requires critical_failure=True; a healthy pipeline with no critical failure is classified STOP_SILENT_FAILURE.
findings.impact: The state machine defines successful evidence handling only for an incident, not normal operation.
findings.improvement: Separate normal success from critical-failure handling; only require blocked=True when critical_failure is true.

findings.issue: Missing evidence_retained routes to ASSIGN_INCIDENT_OWNER even when an owner is already present.
findings.impact: The remediation code points to the wrong missing control.
findings.improvement: Use RETAIN_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE (or equivalent) for evidence absence and ASSIGN_INCIDENT_OWNER only when owner is absent.

findings.issue: logs_redacted, owner and evidence_retained are self-attested fields rather than inspection of retained evidence.
findings.impact: Auditability is represented by claims about auditability.
findings.improvement: Inspect a redacted log fixture, evidence manifest and ownership record.

findings.issue: All eight triads repeat nearly the same E1 inverted predicate -> E2 valid/adversarial/missing dict -> E3 fail-closed classifier grammar.
findings.impact: Learners can master the exercise template without mastering CI/CD or supply-chain operations.
findings.improvement: Diversify tasks: edit YAML, inspect logs, compare artifacts, verify attestation, diagnose environment protection, execute rollback evidence.

findings.issue: Most E3 tasks reuse the same fixture/schema and do not meaningfully change context, contrary to the roadmap's transfer requirement.
findings.impact: The apparent gradual release does not test structural transfer.
findings.improvement: Change repository/workflow/evidence representation and require the learner to select the relevant control without being told the gate name.

findings.issue: All eight demos are local-python simulations although the roadmap specifies controlled CI/cloud for S44.
findings.impact: Worked examples never model the target procedure that You Do asks the learner to produce.
findings.improvement: Introduce at least one complete real CI run worked example, then fade pieces across subsequent exercises.

findings.issue: Legacy id multimodal still renders 'Practica CLIP y Whisper (simulado)' with obsolete multimodal content inside S44 Theory.
findings.impact: Direct learner-facing topic contamination and meta/order leak.
findings.improvement: Keep the stable id but replace only its playground mapping with an S44 CI/supply-chain exercise.

findings.issue: Learner-facing prerequisite labels still say S44 multimodal, S45 IaC, S46 GPU computing, S47 opensource.
findings.impact: The capstone path contradicts the current roadmap and teaches the wrong section identities.
findings.improvement: Update display labels while preserving stable IDs/paths.

findings.issue: Local S44 rubric uses 25/20/15/15/15/10 while canonical CP-N4-B rubric uses 35/20/25/20 and a 2.4/3 critical gate.
findings.impact: Because S44 only starts CP-N4-B, a section-specific rubric can be valid, but its current presentation does not clearly distinguish itself from the capstone rubric.
findings.improvement: Label it 'Rúbrica del incremento S44' and explicitly link the canonical S47 capstone rubric.

findings.issue: Self-check asks what demonstrates 'the gate CP-N4-B' inside S44 even though canonical CP-N4-B gate is S47.
findings.impact: Learners can infer that S44 closes the capstone rather than starts it.
findings.improvement: Ask what demonstrates the S44 increment toward CP-N4-B and state that S47 is the final gate.

findings.issue: The S44 bank is current CI/CD content but is dominated by short conceptual multiple-choice recall such as matrix compatibility, caching and artifact purpose rather than evidence interpretation.
findings.impact: Assessment under-samples Level-4 artifact diagnosis/transfer.
findings.improvement: Keep conceptual items but replace several variants with workflow/log/SBOM/provenance snippets requiring a decision and rationale.

findings.issue: Roadmap requires four authentic topic assessments; S44 source exposes selfCheck but no four topic-assessment artifacts in the CourseSection content.
findings.impact: The section does not satisfy the quantified assessment architecture of its own authoritative roadmap.
findings.improvement: Add one integrated authentic assessment after each T1-T4 pair, jointly scoring both subtopics.

findings.issue: Resource list is generally strong but omits direct first-party artifact-attestation, dependency-review and secret-scanning/push-protection pages while including broad generic course links.
findings.impact: Learners must infer key implementation details from less targeted resources.
findings.improvement: Prioritize current GitHub first-party implementation references and SLSA verification guidance; demote generic links.

findings.issue: Spanish prose carries dense unexplained or inconsistently translated ops vocabulary (artifact, provenance, attestation, owner, hold, breach, lead, ops).
findings.impact: Raises extraneous linguistic load for learners using Peruvian Spanish as the instructional language.
findings.improvement: Define each unavoidable term once in Spanish-first form and keep machine identifiers/code words visually distinct.

findings.issue: The prose broadly says dependencies are fixed by immutable SHA rather than version ranges, conflating GitHub Action pinning with normal package locking/hash verification.
findings.impact: Learners may apply Git commit-SHA policy indiscriminately to package dependencies.
findings.improvement: Separate action refs (full commit SHA) from Python/package dependencies (lockfile + exact versions/hashes as supported by the package tool).

findings.issue: The least-privilege model never teaches the explicit permissions needed to generate GitHub artifact attestations, so the T2-A permissions story does not connect to the T2-B provenance operation.
findings.impact: A learner following the model cannot reason about why the attestation job needs narrowly elevated identity/attestation permissions.
findings.improvement: Add a dedicated attestation job example with the exact minimal permissions and explain why elevation is scoped there.

rejected_findings.reason: It is a stable learner URL/progress key; content mapping should change, not the key without migration.

rejected_findings.claim: S44 must deploy to a real public cloud.
rejected_findings.reason: CP-N4-B explicitly permits a scoped local demo; the defect is lack of authentic CI evidence, not lack of paid cloud infrastructure.
Roadmap says S44 starts CP-N4-B; canonical gate is S47.

rejected_findings.claim: Using caches is a reproducibility defect.
rejected_findings.reason: The theory correctly states cache is an optimization and not source of truth.

rejected_findings.claim: Full 40-hex action SHA pinning is overkill.
rejected_findings.reason: GitHub currently documents full-length commit SHA as the immutable pinning control.
